conventions.transaction: Commands run in transactions: all commit or none. Optional expectedVersion fails with version-conflict when the document changed.
conventions.placeholders: A create command may define "ref": "$name"; later commands in the same transaction may use "$name" for the created ID (the first string field of its result) or "$name.field[.index]".
conventions.units: Lengths in mm, angles in degrees. Expressions may use parameters, + - * / % ^, functions (sin, cos, tan in degrees, sqrt, abs, min, max, …) and unit suffixes (mm, cm, m, in, ft, deg, rad).
conventions.errors: Errors are { code, message, details? }; codes are listed per command.
conventions.ids: IDs are deterministic within a document (prefix-counter) and never reused. Global references use the document UUID plus the entity ID.

commands.name: set_document_metadata
commands.summary: Set the document title or description.

commands.name: set_document_source
commands.summary: Record the Conceptualize concept (and optionally the CAD handoff package) this document was started from, at an exact revision. Provenance only: nothing is copied; when the concept is revised later the document can be reported as possibly outdated, and it is never regenerated automatically.

revision.description: Concept revision the document is based on.

label.description: Display text captured now (not authoritative), e.g. "CON-012 Bit holder".

preconditions: revision is a positive integer.

commands.name: clear_document_source
commands.summary: Remove the recorded source concept of the document.
preconditions: A source is recorded.

commands.name: create_part
commands.summary: Create an empty part (a container for parameters and a feature history).

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.name: rename
commands.summary: Rename a part or feature (display name only; IDs never change).
preconditions: The part or feature exists.

commands.name: set_material
commands.summary: Set the material of a part (used for mass properties).
preconditions: The part exists.

commands.name: create_parameter
commands.summary: Create a named design parameter with an expression.

expression.description: Value. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The name is a valid identifier, not reserved (functions, constants, units) and unique in the part.
The expression only uses existing parameters and creates no cycle.

commands.name: set_parameter
commands.summary: Change a parameter’s expression; dependent sketches and features regenerate.

expression.description: New value. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

preconditions: The parameter exists.
The expression only uses existing parameters and creates no cycle.

commands.name: delete_parameter
commands.summary: Delete an unused parameter.
preconditions: No parameter, dimension or feature uses it.

commands.name: create_sketch
commands.summary: Create an empty sketch on a standard plane (XY, XZ or YZ), a datum plane or a planar face (by stable name), optionally offset along its normal.

datum.description: A datum plane of the part (create_datum_plane).

face.description: Stable name of a planar face, e.g. "ext-5/cap-end" (query get_entities).

offset.description: Offset along the plane normal. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The part exists.
Exactly one of plane, datum or face is given; a datum is a datum plane earlier in the part; a face names a face of an earlier feature (planarity is checked at regeneration).

commands.name: set_sketch_plane
commands.summary: Move a sketch to another standard plane, datum plane or planar face, or change its offset.

datum.description: A datum plane of the part (create_datum_plane).

face.description: Stable name of a planar face, e.g. "ext-5/cap-end" (query get_entities).

offset.description: Offset along the plane normal. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

preconditions: The sketch exists.
Exactly one of plane, datum or face; references must come earlier in the history than the sketch.

commands.name: create_datum_plane
commands.summary: Create a datum (reference) plane: a standard plane, another datum plane or a planar face, offset along its normal. Sketches can be placed on it.

datum.description: A datum plane of the part (create_datum_plane).

face.description: Stable name of a planar face, e.g. "ext-5/cap-end" (query get_entities).

offset.description: Offset along the plane normal. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: Exactly one of plane, datum or face; references must exist earlier in the part.

commands.name: add_point
commands.summary: Add a point to a sketch.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The sketch exists.

commands.name: add_line
commands.summary: Add a line segment between two points (existing point IDs or new coordinates).

oneOf.description: ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")
ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")

construction.description: Construction lines are ignored by profiles (e.g. revolution axes).

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.name: add_circle
commands.summary: Add a circle (centre point and seed radius). Add a radius or diameter constraint to fix its size.

oneOf.description: ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.name: add_arc
commands.summary: Add a circular arc, counter-clockwise from start to end around the centre.

oneOf.description: ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")
ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")
ID of an existing sketch point (or "origin")

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.name: add_rectangle
commands.summary: Add an axis-aligned rectangle: four lines with coincident corners, horizontal/vertical constraints and (by default) width and height dimensions.

corner.description: Lower-left corner [x, y] (default [0, 0]); the corner is fixed to the origin when it is [0, 0].

center.description: Centre [x, y] instead of a corner.

width.description: Width (x). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

height.description: Height (y). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

dimensions.description: Add driving width and height dimensions.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.output: { points: [4], lines: [bottom, right, top, left], constraints: [...], width?: constraintId, height?: constraintId }
preconditions: The sketch exists; width and height are positive.

commands.name: add_regular_polygon
commands.summary: Add a regular polygon as editable sketch geometry: N lines with equal-length and point-on-circle constraints on a construction circumcircle, its centre dimensioned from the origin, its rotation fixed, and its size as a driving dimension (across flats through a tangent inscribed construction circle, or the circumradius). Fully constrained; the solver checks it like any sketch.

center.description: Centre [x, y] in mm (default [0, 0]); dimensioned from the origin.

acrossFlats.description: Distance between opposite sides (inscribed-circle diameter). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

circumradius.description: Distance from the centre to a vertex. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

rotation.description: Angle of the first vertex from the sketch x axis, in degrees (default 0). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

name.description: Name of the size dimension (default "across flats" or "circumradius").

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

commands.output: { points: [N], lines: [N], center, circumcircle, inscribedCircle?, size: constraintId, constraints: [...] }
preconditions: The sketch exists.
Exactly one of size.acrossFlats and size.circumradius is given, and it is positive.
Rotation is a number or expression in degrees.
commands.undo: Removes the polygon and its constraints.

commands.name: apply_constraint
commands.summary: Apply a geometric or dimensional constraint to sketch entities.

entities.description: Entity IDs in the order the type defines (see the constraint reference); "origin", "x-axis" and "y-axis" are always available.

value.description: Dimensional constraints only. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

driving.description: false: a driven (reference) dimension that only measures.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The entities exist and match the constraint signature.
A driving dimension has a value; length, radius and diameter are positive.

commands.name: set_dimension
commands.summary: Change the value of a dimensional constraint (a literal or an expression); the sketch and dependent features regenerate.

value.description: New value. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

preconditions: The constraint exists and is dimensional.

commands.name: set_dimension_driving
commands.summary: Switch a dimension between driving (solved for) and driven (reference, measured only).
preconditions: The constraint is dimensional; a driving dimension has a value.

commands.name: delete_constraint
commands.summary: Remove a constraint from a sketch.
preconditions: The constraint exists.

commands.name: delete_sketch_entities
commands.summary: Delete sketch entities; curves using deleted points and constraints referring to deleted entities are removed too.
preconditions: Every ID exists in the sketch (implicit origin and axes cannot be deleted).
commands.undo: Restores all removed entities and constraints.

commands.name: move_sketch_point
commands.summary: Move a point’s drawn (seed) position; constraints still decide the solved position.
preconditions: The point exists.

commands.name: set_construction
commands.summary: Mark sketch curves as construction geometry (excluded from profiles) or normal geometry.
preconditions: Every ID is a line, circle or arc of the sketch.

commands.name: extrude_profile
commands.summary: Extrude the closed profile of a sketch along its normal: a new body, joined to a body, or cut from it.

distance.description: Extrusion depth (> 0). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

operation.description: new body, join (fuse) or cut. The first solid of a part is always a new body.

target.description: Body to join or cut (ID of the feature that created it). Default: the latest body.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The sketch exists; a literal distance is > 0; an explicit target is a body-creating feature earlier in the part.

commands.name: revolve_profile
commands.summary: Revolve the closed profile of a sketch about a sketch line or a sketch axis.

axis.description: A line of the sketch (often construction), or "x-axis" / "y-axis".

angle.description: Angle in degrees, (0, 360]. Default 360. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The axis is a line of the sketch or a sketch axis; a literal angle is in (0, 360].

commands.name: fillet_edges
commands.summary: Round edges of a body with a constant radius. Edges are selected by stable edge names (query get_entities).

radius.description: Fillet radius (> 0). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

target.description: Body (ID of the feature that created it). Default: the latest body.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: A body exists (checked at regeneration).
A literal radius is > 0.
Edge names resolve on the body at regeneration; otherwise the feature fails with reason reference-lost.

commands.name: chamfer_edges
commands.summary: Bevel edges of a body with an equal-distance chamfer. Edges are selected by stable edge names (query get_entities).

distance.description: Chamfer distance (> 0). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

target.description: Body (ID of the feature that created it). Default: the latest body.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: A body exists (checked at regeneration).
A literal distance is > 0.
Edge names resolve on the body at regeneration; otherwise the feature fails with reason reference-lost.

commands.name: edit_feature
commands.summary: Change a feature: extrude (distance, direction), revolve (angle, axis), fillet (radius, edges), chamfer (distance, edges), datum plane (offset), linear pattern (count, spacing, direction, features); operation or target body.

distance.description: Extrude depth or chamfer distance. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

direction.description: Extrude: normal, reverse or symmetric. Linear pattern: an axis name ("x", "-y" …) or an [x, y, z] vector.

angle.description: Revolve angle. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

target.description: Body to join, cut, fillet or chamfer; null for the latest body.

radius.description: Fillet radius. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

edges.description: Fillet or chamfer edges (stable edge names).

offset.description: Datum plane offset. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

count.description: Linear pattern: number of occurrences including the original (integer ≥ 2). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

spacing.description: Linear pattern: distance between neighbouring occurrences. A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

features.description: Linear pattern: extrude or revolve features to repeat.

preconditions: Only the fields of the feature type are given; values are valid.

commands.name: pattern_linear
commands.summary: Repeat extrude or revolve features (for example a pocket cut) along a direction: count occurrences (including the original), spacing apart. Count and spacing may be expressions over parameters. Each occurrence is rebuilt from the original sketch on a shifted plane and applied with the same operation; faces get stable names "<patternId>/i<k>-<featureId>-<role>". Regeneration reports the gap between neighbouring occurrences.

features.description: Extrude or revolve feature IDs, earlier in the same part.

direction.description: Model direction: "x", "y", "z", "-x", "-y", "-z", or an [x, y, z] vector (normalised).

count.description: Number of occurrences including the original (integer ≥ 2). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

spacing.description: Distance between neighbouring occurrences (mm, > 0). A number in document units (mm, deg) or an expression over part parameters, e.g. "width / 2" or "1 in".

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The features are extrudes or revolves of the same part, earlier in the history.
count evaluates to an integer ≥ 2 and spacing to a positive length (checked again at regeneration).

commands.name: bind_parameter
commands.summary: Record what a parameter implements: a revision-pinned reference to another module's artifact (typically a design constraint, { module: "conceptualize", kind: "constraint", id, revision }). Nothing is copied from the target; cad-modeler.check reads the bound values from the owning module, and cad-modeler.check_bindings reports bindings pinned to superseded revisions.

revision.description: The target revision the parameter was set against.

quantity.description: The quantity of the target the parameter implements (e.g. "pocket across flats").

preconditions: The parameter exists.

commands.name: unbind_parameter
commands.summary: Remove the binding of a parameter (its value and expression stay).
preconditions: The parameter exists and is bound.

commands.name: set_suppressed
commands.summary: Suppress or unsuppress a feature (suppressed features are skipped by regeneration; dependents are blocked).
preconditions: The feature exists.

commands.name: delete_feature
commands.summary: Delete a feature that no other feature depends on.
preconditions: No later feature uses the sketch or targets the body.
No semantic annotation or external reference uses it.

commands.name: add_semantic
commands.summary: Annotate faces, features or parameters with engineering meaning (named interface, functional surface, design intent).

targets.description: Stable face names (e.g. "ext-5/cap-end"), feature or parameter IDs.

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: Feature and parameter targets exist; face names start with an existing feature ID.

commands.name: remove_semantic
commands.summary: Remove an engineering annotation.
preconditions: The annotation exists.

commands.name: repair_reference
commands.summary: Replace one lost face or edge reference of a feature (fillet or chamfer edge, or the face or datum a sketch or datum plane sits on) by a replacement chosen by the person or an approved proposal. Nothing is re-bound automatically: the replacement is given explicitly (see query get_reference_repairs for the lost names and the candidates).

featureId.description: Feature ID of the fillet, chamfer, sketch or datum plane with the lost reference

from.description: The lost reference, exactly as stored in the feature (an edge name, or a face name).

to.description: The replacement: an existing edge name (fillet, chamfer) or face name (sketch, datum plane). It is checked when the model regenerates; use a dry run to preview.

preconditions: The feature stores the reference “from” (fillet, chamfer: in its edge list; sketch, datum plane: as its face).
“to” differs from “from” and is not already in the feature.
The replacement is checked at regeneration; if it does not resolve, the feature reports reference-lost again.

commands.name: add_reference
commands.summary: Link a CAD entity to an artifact of another module (Project Management product element, twin component, requirement, SysML element, Concept). The target is referenced, never copied.

subject.description: Part, feature, parameter or face name

revision.description: Pin a revision; omit to follow the latest.

label.description: Display text captured when linking (not authoritative).

ref.description: Placeholder ("$name") that later commands in the same transaction can use instead of the new ID.

preconditions: The subject exists in the document.
The target is validated by the caller against the owning module (the UI does; the assistant receives its result).

commands.name: remove_reference
commands.summary: Remove a cross-module reference.
preconditions: The reference exists.

queries.name: get_feature_tree
queries.summary: Parts, feature history in order, status, errors, warnings and dependencies of each feature.

queries.name: get_parameters
queries.summary: Parameters of a part with expressions, evaluated values, errors and users.

queries.name: get_sketch
queries.summary: Sketch entities (drawn and solved positions), constraints with values, constraint status, degrees of freedom, free points, redundant/conflicting constraints and closed profiles.

queries.name: get_entities
queries.summary: Faces and edges of the bodies with stable names, surface/curve types, areas, lengths, centres and normals.

queries.name: get_mass_properties
queries.summary: Volume, surface area, centre of mass, bounding box and (with a material) mass of each body.

queries.name: get_dependencies
queries.summary: Dependency graph: parameter → parameter/feature, sketch → feature, body chain.

queries.name: get_failures
queries.summary: Regeneration failures, blocked features, warnings and parameter errors.

queries.name: get_reference_repairs
queries.summary: Features with a lost face or edge reference (reference-lost): the lost names and candidate replacements, best name matches first. Candidates are suggestions; repair_reference applies only the replacement a person or an approved proposal names.

queries.name: get_regeneration_summary
queries.summary: Last regeneration: version, duration, kernel, rebuilt and reused features, body validity.

queries.name: get_operation_log
queries.summary: Recent committed, rejected, undone and redone transactions with source and affected IDs.

queries.name: list_commands
queries.summary: The machine-readable command catalogue (names, input schemas, preconditions, errors).

sessionOperations.name: undo
sessionOperations.summary: Restore the state before the last transaction (a new version).

sessionOperations.name: redo
sessionOperations.summary: Re-apply an undone transaction (a new version).

sessionOperations.name: regenerate_model
sessionOperations.summary: Regenerate the whole model; with full: true the cache is cleared first.

sessionOperations.name: dry_run
sessionOperations.summary: Execute a transaction and regenerate on a copy: predicted statuses and mass properties, nothing committed.

sessionOperations.name: export_step
sessionOperations.summary: Export the bodies of a part as STEP AP242 (exact B-rep, names, units, colours).

sessionOperations.name: save_document / open_document
sessionOperations.summary: Serialise or load the native ews-cad JSON file.
